properties.name: Use a startupProbe for slow-starting applications
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Set -XX:MaxRAMPercentage on the JVM or --max-old-space-size on Node. A runtime that reads host memory will size itself far above the container limit and be killed while believing it has room.
properties.name: Size the runtime heap from the cgroup limit
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: minAvailable must be below the replica count, or ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS is zero and every drain and node upgrade stalls forever. A PDB on a single-replica workload is always unsatisfiable.
properties.name: Set PodDisruptionBudgets that can actually be satisfied
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Defers volume creation until the pod is scheduled, so the volume lands in an AZ that has capacity. Immediate binding is how a pod ends up permanently unschedulable next to its own disk.
properties.name: Use volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A bare pod has nothing to recreate it, so drain refuses to evict it and any node replacement loses it permanently.
properties.name: Run every workload under a controller, never as a bare pod
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: kube-reserved and system-reserved keep pods from consuming the memory the node itself needs. Without them a busy node takes the kubelet down and goes NotReady.
properties.name: Reserve resources for the kubelet and the OS
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: targetPort: http survives a port renumbering; targetPort: 8080 silently breaks when the container moves.
properties.name: Name container ports and reference the name in Services
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: In Helm or Kustomize, generate both from one source. Hand-maintained selectors drift and silently empty the Service.
properties.name: Derive Service selectors from the same labels the template sets
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: One role per service account, least privilege. The node instance role is shared by every pod on the node, so granting there grants to everything.
properties.name: Give each workload its own IRSA role, scoped to what it uses
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Without the provider the projected token cannot be exchanged and the annotation is ignored silently — the pod falls back to the node role and appears to work until it hits a permission the node role lacks.
properties.name: Create the cluster's IAM OIDC provider before any IRSA annotation
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: eksctl create iamserviceaccount, or a Terraform module that emits both. The trust policy's sub condition and the annotation must agree exactly, and hand-editing one of the two is the usual break.
properties.name: Manage service accounts and their roles together
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: State stores every attribute in plaintext, including generated passwords and private keys. S3 with SSE-KMS, versioning and blocked public access; DynamoDB for locking.
properties.name: Never commit Terraform state, and encrypt the bucket
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Kubernetes networking is allow-all until a policy selects a pod. A default-deny plus explicit allows makes lateral movement a deliberate decision.
properties.name: Default-deny NetworkPolicy per namespace
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: PodSecurityPolicy was removed in 1.25. The replacement is Pod Security Admission labels on the namespace, or an admission controller like Kyverno for anything more expressive.
properties.name: Enforce Pod Security Standards at the namespace level
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: IMDSv1 lets any pod that can make an HTTP request read the node role's credentials. Hop limit 1 stops containers reaching the metadata endpoint at all.
properties.name: Require IMDSv2 and hop limit 1 on nodes
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Secrets are base64, not encrypted. EKS envelope encryption with a customer-managed KMS key is what makes 'Secret' mean anything against etcd access.
properties.name: Encrypt Kubernetes secrets at rest with a KMS key
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The default is never expire. Log groups created by controllers and Lambda inherit it and bill indefinitely.
properties.name: Put a retention policy on every CloudWatch log group
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: NAT gateways bill per hour and per gigabyte. Image pulls and S3 traffic through NAT is one of the most common surprise line items on an EKS bill, and endpoints remove it entirely.
properties.name: Route S3 and ECR through VPC endpoints, not NAT
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Requests set once during development and never revisited are the main source of over-provisioning, because the scheduler reserves them whether or not they are used.
properties.name: Right-size from observed usage, not from the first guess
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Multiple instance types across AZs, with a handler that drains on the two-minute notice. Single-type Spot pools are what makes people distrust Spot.
properties.name: Run interruption-tolerant workloads on Spot with a diversified pool
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A Retain reclaim policy leaves the volume behind when the PVC goes, and it bills forever. Released PVs are the usual culprit.
properties.name: Delete unattached EBS volumes and old snapshots
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A named installation of a chart, with revision history stored as Secrets in its namespace.
properties.gotcha: Deleting a release does not delete PVCs created from StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates.
properties.name: HelmRelease

properties.doc: Endpoint, status, multi-AZ, parameter group and the pending-modified values that a maintenance window will apply.
properties.name: aws rds describe-db-instances

properties.doc: The resource policy. Where a cross-account denial is usually proven or ruled out.
properties.name: aws s3api get-bucket-policy

properties.doc: Key state and rotation. A key pending deletion makes everything encrypted with it unreadable when the window closes.
properties.name: aws kms describe-key

properties.doc: Which AWS services are reachable privately. On a private cluster the absence of ecr.api, ecr.dkr, s3, sts and logs endpoints explains nodes that never join.
properties.name: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints

properties.doc: Free IPs per subnet and the tags. AvailableIpAddressCount near zero is why pods stop getting addresses; missing role/elb tags are why load balancers never provision.
properties.name: aws ec2 describe-subnets

properties.doc: Records in a zone; confirms whether ExternalDNS actually wrote what you expect.
properties.name: aws route53 list-resource-record-sets

properties.doc: The AWS CNI gives every pod a real VPC IP from the node's ENIs, so pods are first-class VPC citizens reachable by security groups and load balancers with no overlay.
properties.gotcha: Pods per node are capped by (ENIs x IPs per ENI) - 1, a function of instance type. An m5.large tops out at 29 pods however much CPU is free.
properties.name: VPCCNI
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Assigns each ENI a /28 prefix instead of individual IPs, raising the pod ceiling roughly 16x without changing instance type.
properties.gotcha: Needs contiguous /28 blocks. A fragmented subnet cannot allocate them and silently falls back to the old density.
properties.name: PrefixDelegation
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Places pods in different subnets from the nodes, usually a secondary CIDR, when the primary subnets are exhausted.
properties.gotcha: Costs one ENI's worth of addresses per node and disables the node's primary ENI for pods, lowering max pods further.
properties.name: CustomNetworking
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Assigns a security group per pod via branch ENIs, so a pod can be granted RDS access without granting the whole node.
properties.gotcha: Only on nitro instance types, and each pod using it consumes a branch ENI from a limited pool.
properties.name: SecurityGroupsForPods
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: kube-proxy writes one iptables chain per Service and picks a backend by random probability. The default.
properties.gotcha: Rule evaluation is O(n) in Services; several thousand Services makes rule sync and packet handling measurably slow.
properties.name: IptablesMode
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Uses the kernel's IPVS hash tables instead of linear iptables chains — O(1) lookup, real scheduling algorithms (rr, lc, sh).
properties.gotcha: Needs the ip_vs kernel modules loaded on every node; without them kube-proxy silently falls back to iptables.
properties.name: IPVSMode
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The cluster DNS server, normally two replicas serving every pod's lookups.
properties.gotcha: Two replicas for a whole cluster is the default and is frequently the bottleneck. Scale it with the node count, and keep replicas on different nodes.
properties.name: CoreDNS
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A DaemonSet caching DNS on each node, so lookups never leave the host in the common case.
properties.gotcha: The standard fix for DNS latency and conntrack pressure at scale; not installed by default on EKS.
properties.name: NodeLocalDNSCache
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The default resolv.conf sets ndots:5, so any name with fewer than five dots is tried against every search domain first. 'api.example.com' becomes four failed lookups before the right one.
properties.gotcha: The single most common cause of mysterious DNS latency in Kubernetes. A trailing dot on the name, or a per-pod dnsConfig with ndots:1, removes it.
properties.name: NdotsFive
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The kernel tracks every connection for NAT and stateful filtering, in a table with a fixed maximum.
properties.gotcha: When it fills, new connections are dropped silently and the only evidence is 'nf_conntrack: table full' in dmesg. Symptoms look like random application timeouts.
properties.name: ConntrackTable
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A NAT gateway supports about 55,000 simultaneous connections to a single destination IP:port, because it must allocate a source port per connection.
properties.gotcha: Many pods calling one external API through one NAT gateway hit this and see intermittent connection failures long before any bandwidth limit.
properties.name: SNATPortExhaustion
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: AWS supports 9001-byte jumbo frames inside a VPC, but 1500 across peering to some destinations and over VPN.
properties.gotcha: A path MTU mismatch shows up as large transfers hanging while small requests succeed — TLS handshake fine, first big response stalls.
properties.name: MTU
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Direct one-to-one VPC connection, no transitive routing.
properties.gotcha: Not transitive: A-B and B-C does not give A-C. CIDRs must not overlap, ever.
properties.name: VPCPeering
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Hub-and-spoke routing between many VPCs and on-premises, with route tables per attachment.
properties.gotcha: Charged per attachment per hour plus per GB; the usual answer once peering becomes a mesh.
properties.name: TransitGateway
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Exposes a single service across accounts without routing between VPCs, so CIDRs may overlap.
properties.gotcha: One endpoint per service per VPC, and it is unidirectional — the consumer initiates, never the provider.
properties.name: PrivateLink
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Adds pod IP and node to the listing. Confirms whether pods actually received addresses and how they are spread across nodes and AZs.
properties.name: kubectl get pods -o wide
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Resolves a name from inside the pod's own DNS config, which is the only place the search-domain and ndots behaviour is visible. Resolving from your laptop proves nothing.
properties.name: kubectl exec dns lookup
properties.source: curated operational knowledge
properties.syntax: kubectl exec -it POD -- nslookup NAME   # or dig +search +short NAME

properties.doc: A throwaway pod with dig, curl, tcpdump, ss, conntrack and iperf. The standard way to test connectivity from inside the pod network rather than from outside it.
properties.name: kubectl run netshoot
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The VPC CNI's own log. IP allocation failures, ENI attach errors and warm-pool exhaustion are reported here and nowhere else.
properties.example: kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=aws-node --tail=100 | grep -i 'no available ip'
properties.name: kubectl logs aws-node
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: CoreDNS errors, upstream failures and (with the log plugin enabled) per-query timing.
properties.name: kubectl logs coredns
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Which policies select which pods. Remember the rule: a pod with no policy selecting it accepts everything; as soon as one selects it, that direction becomes default-deny.
properties.name: kubectl get networkpolicy
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Per-CPU connection-tracking statistics. A non-zero and rising insert_failed or drop is conntrack table pressure, which presents to applications as random timeouts.
properties.example: aws ssm start-session --target i-0abc  # then: sudo conntrack -S
properties.name: conntrack -S
properties.source: curated operational knowledge
properties.syntax: conntrack -S   # on the node, via ssm or kubectl debug node

properties.doc: Packet capture inside the pod's network namespace. Settles 'did the request even leave' and 'did anything come back' when logs on both sides disagree.
properties.example: kubectl debug -it checkout-x2k --image=nicolaka/netshoot --target=app -- tcpdump -ni any port 5432
properties.name: tcpdump in a pod
properties.source: curated operational knowledge
properties.syntax: kubectl debug -it POD --image=nicolaka/netshoot --target=C -- tcpdump -ni any port 443

properties.doc: Shows selector, ports with targetPort, sessionAffinity, externalTrafficPolicy and the cloud annotations. externalTrafficPolicy: Local preserves the client IP but blackholes traffic on nodes with no local pod.
properties.example: kubectl get svc checkout -n prod -o yaml
properties.name: kubectl get svc -o yaml
properties.source: curated operational knowledge
properties.syntax: kubectl get svc NAME -n NS -o yaml

properties.doc: ENIs attached to a node and the secondary IPs on each. This is the ground truth for pod-density limits and for IP exhaustion.
properties.name: aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: NAT gateways and their state. Pair with the ErrorPortAllocation CloudWatch metric, which is the only direct evidence of SNAT port exhaustion.
properties.name: aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: no available ip addresses failed to assign an IP cni error pods stuck containercreating ip exhaustion subnet full enis full max pods reached
properties.doc: Pods stay Pending or ContainerCreating with a CNI failure to assign an address. Two different ceilings look identical: the node is out of ENI slots, or the subnet is out of free IPs.
properties.name: PodIPExhaustion
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Max pods is (ENIs x IPs per ENI) - 1 for the instance type, independent of CPU and memory. A node with idle CPU can still be full.
properties.name: Node reached its ENI-based pod limit
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Enable prefix delegation, or use a larger instance type
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: AvailableIpAddressCount is at or near zero. Every node in that subnet stops placing pods at once, so it looks like a cluster-wide failure.
properties.name: Subnet has no free addresses
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Add a secondary CIDR with custom networking, or move to larger subnets
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: WARM_IP_TARGET and MINIMUM_IP_TARGET control how many addresses the CNI keeps ready. Tuned too low, a scale-up outruns allocation and pods wait on the AWS API.
properties.name: Warm IP pool too small for burst scaling
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Raise WARM_IP_TARGET / MINIMUM_IP_TARGET on the aws-node DaemonSet
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: dns not resolving slow dns intermittent name resolution 5 second delay timeouts resolving service name coredns failing nxdomain lookup slow
properties.doc: Intermittent name resolution failures or requests that are mysteriously slow by exactly 5 seconds. Almost never the DNS server being down; almost always search-domain amplification or resolver timeouts.
properties.name: DNSLatencyOrFailure
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Any name with fewer than five dots is tried against each search domain first, so an external name costs four NXDOMAINs before the real answer. Multiply by every request and CoreDNS is saturated by queries that were never going to resolve.
properties.name: ndots:5 turns one lookup into five
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Use a fully-qualified name with a trailing dot, or set dnsConfig ndots:1 on the pod
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The default two replicas serve every pod in the cluster. Beyond a few hundred nodes that is the bottleneck, and the symptom is latency rather than failure.
properties.name: CoreDNS under-replicated for the cluster size
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Scale CoreDNS with cluster size and spread it with anti-affinity
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The classic 5-second delay: glibc sends A and AAAA queries in parallel from one socket, and a conntrack insert race drops one. The resolver waits its full timeout before retrying.
properties.name: Conntrack races on parallel UDP lookups
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Deploy NodeLocalDNSCache so lookups use TCP to a local cache
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A default-deny egress policy that forgets UDP 53 to the kube-system namespace breaks DNS for every selected pod, while everything else appears configured correctly.
properties.name: A NetworkPolicy denies egress to kube-dns
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Add an explicit egress allow to kube-dns on UDP and TCP 53
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: random connection timeouts nf_conntrack table full packet drops intermittent failures under load connection reset no route
properties.doc: Connections are dropped once the kernel's connection-tracking table fills. Applications see random timeouts with no error anywhere in Kubernetes, because the packet never reaches userspace.
properties.name: ConntrackTableFull
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Short-lived outbound connections at high rate, each held in the table for the timeout after closing. nf_conntrack_max is sized from node memory and is often far too small for a busy node.
properties.name: Connection churn exceeds the table size
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Raise nf_conntrack_max and lower the TIME_WAIT timeout on the nodes
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A new TCP connection per request multiplies table pressure by the request rate. The fix is in the client, not the kernel.
properties.name: No connection pooling in the application
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Enable keep-alive and connection pooling in the client
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: intermittent outbound failures nat gateway errors cannot reach external api connection refused sporadic errorportallocation
properties.doc: Outbound connections to one destination start failing intermittently while bandwidth is nowhere near any limit. A NAT gateway can hold about 55,000 simultaneous connections to a single destination IP and port.
properties.name: SNATPortExhaustion
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Every pod shares the gateway's source addresses, so they collectively exhaust the port space toward that one destination. The CloudWatch ErrorPortAllocation metric is the direct evidence.
properties.name: Many pods calling one external endpoint through one NAT gateway
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Add a NAT gateway per AZ, or reach the service privately via a VPC endpoint or PrivateLink
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Each request opening a fresh connection consumes a port for the duration plus the timeout.
properties.name: No connection reuse to the external service
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Pool and reuse connections in the client
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: 502 from alb targets unhealthy load balancer cannot reach pods health check failing target group draining nlb timeout
properties.doc: The load balancer exists and the pods are Ready, but targets are unhealthy so traffic 502s or times out. The disagreement is between what Kubernetes considers healthy and what the load balancer can actually reach.
properties.name: LoadBalancerTargetsUnhealthy
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: In IP target mode the load balancer connects straight to the pod IP. If the node or pod security group does not allow the LB subnets on that port, every check fails while the pod is perfectly healthy.
properties.name: Pod security group does not allow the health-check port from the load balancer
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Allow the health-check port from the load balancer's security group or subnet CIDRs
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The default path is / and many services answer 404 there while /healthz is fine.
properties.name: Health-check path returns non-2xx
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Point the health check at the real readiness path
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: In instance target mode with Local, nodes without a local pod fail the check by design. That is correct behaviour that looks like a broken cluster.
properties.name: externalTrafficPolicy Local with no pod on some nodes
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Use IP target mode, or run the workload as a DaemonSet, or accept the partial target set
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: cannot connect after network policy traffic blocked pods cannot talk to each other connection refused between namespaces egress denied
properties.doc: Traffic that used to work stops after a policy is applied somewhere in the namespace. The rule that surprises people: a pod nothing selects allows everything, but the moment any policy selects it, that direction becomes default-deny.
properties.name: NetworkPolicyBlocksTraffic
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Someone adds an ingress policy for one app; every pod its selector happens to match now denies all other ingress. The team that broke it and the team that notices are usually different.
properties.name: An unrelated policy made the pod default-deny
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Narrow the selector, or add the missing explicit allows
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A default-deny egress without UDP and TCP 53 to kube-dns breaks name resolution for every selected pod, and the symptom looks like DNS trouble rather than policy.
properties.name: Egress policy omits DNS
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Always pair a default-deny egress with an explicit kube-dns allow
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: namespaceSelector matches labels on the Namespace object, not its name. An unlabelled namespace matches nothing and the rule silently allows nobody.
properties.name: Policy uses namespaceSelector without the namespace being labelled
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Label the namespace, or use kubernetes.io/metadata.name
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: large requests hang small requests work transfer stalls tls handshake ok then nothing mtu path discovery broken
properties.doc: Small requests succeed and large transfers hang. The TLS handshake completes, then the first large response never arrives — a packet too big to forward is dropped and the ICMP that should say so is filtered.
properties.name: MTUBlackhole
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The VPC supports 9001 inside, but a peering link, VPN or internet path takes 1500. Without working path MTU discovery the oversized packets vanish.
properties.name: Path MTU smaller than the pod interface MTU
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Lower the CNI MTU to the smallest path, or allow ICMP fragmentation-needed through
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.aliases: data transfer costs high cross az charges latency between pods expensive network bill inter-zone traffic
properties.doc: Latency and the data-transfer bill both climb because traffic crosses availability zones on almost every hop. Nothing is broken; the topology is simply ignored by default.
properties.name: CrossAZTrafficCost
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: By default a Service picks any ready endpoint, so roughly two thirds of traffic leaves the zone in a three-AZ cluster, and every crossing is billed in both directions.
properties.name: Service routing ignores zone
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Enable topology-aware routing on the Service, and spread replicas with zone topology constraints
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Default-deny semantics misunderstood
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Topology ignored by default
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.name: Connection not reused
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Two CoreDNS replicas is a default, not a sizing decision. A per-node cache removes most cross-node DNS traffic and the conntrack races that cause the 5-second stalls.
properties.name: Deploy NodeLocalDNSCache and scale CoreDNS with the cluster
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: The ndots:5 default turns every short external name into four wasted lookups. Fixing it is a one-line dnsConfig and often the single largest DNS win.
properties.name: Set ndots:1 or fully-qualify external names
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: A default-deny that forgets UDP/TCP 53 to kube-dns breaks name resolution for every pod it selects, and presents as a DNS outage rather than a policy change.
properties.name: Pair every default-deny egress policy with an explicit DNS allow
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Max pods per node is a property of the instance type, and subnet size caps the cluster. Both are painful to change later — a subnet cannot be resized, only supplemented.
properties.name: Plan pod density and subnet size before the cluster exists
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Cross-AZ transfer is billed in both directions and adds latency. Zone-aware routing keeps traffic local when a local endpoint exists.
properties.name: Enable topology-aware routing and spread replicas across zones
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Removes both the per-GB NAT charge and the SNAT port ceiling for that destination in one change.
properties.name: Reach AWS services through VPC endpoints rather than NAT
properties.source: curated operational knowledge

properties.doc: Lets a single pod reach RDS without granting the whole node, which is the usual over-permission in EKS networking.
properties.name: Use security groups for pods when a workload needs its own network identity
properties.source: curated operational knowledge
